pr_title: Preserve new lines and whitespace when adding secret
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/19298

Summary of the changes
- Preserve existing formatting of project file when loading
- Manually insert spacing and new line when adding `UserSecretsId` element to project file (necessary because we've indicated that whitespace should be preserved)
- Replace existing `using` statement with C# 8 using declaration
- Add a unit test to confirm that the modified project file (with the `UserSecretsId` element) contains exactly 1 more line

Project file before:

```xml
<Project ToolsVersion="15.0" Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFrameworks>netcoreapp5.0</TargetFrameworks>
    
    <EnableDefaultCompileItems>false</EnableDefaultCompileItems>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="**\*.cs" Exclude="Excluded.cs;$(DefaultItemExcludes)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Project file after:

```xml
<Project ToolsVersion="15.0" Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFrameworks>netcoreapp5.0</TargetFrameworks>
    
    <EnableDefaultCompileItems>false</EnableDefaultCompileItems>
    <UserSecretsId>06af5cc9-a276-4fbe-b65c-5bbd10f5280c</UserSecretsId>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="**\*.cs" Exclude="Excluded.cs;$(DefaultItemExcludes)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

issue_context.title: User secrets init does not preserve whitespace/newlines
issue_context.body:
User secrets init does not preserve whitespace/newlines.
As well as that it currently adds an xml declaration (which is fixed in 5.0) it also removes all newlines from the file.

Should it be as simple as ?
```cs
new XDocument(projectPath, LoadOptions.PreserveWhitespace)
new XmlWriterSettings { NewLineHandling = NewLineHandling.None }
```

Related to https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/14354 @scottaddie

review_comments: I'm not seeing an indentation problem when I run the GA version of the tool. Is this necessary?

It's necessary to properly indent the `UserSecretsId` element. That's now necessary because we're respecting whitespace when loading the XML doc. Without it, we end up with the following after adding the `UserSecretsId` element:

```xml
<Project ToolsVersion="15.0" Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFrameworks>netcoreapp5.0</TargetFrameworks>
    
    <EnableDefaultCompileItems>false</EnableDefaultCompileItems>
  <UserSecretsId>23ffe3ee-814e-4f18-987e-7f7ab65ae0ab</UserSecretsId></PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="**\*.cs" Exclude="Excluded.cs;$(DefaultItemExcludes)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```
Same here, do we need to explicitly add a newline?

Without it, we end up with the following after adding the `UserSecretsId` element:

```xml
<Project ToolsVersion="15.0" Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFrameworks>netcoreapp5.0</TargetFrameworks>
    
    <EnableDefaultCompileItems>false</EnableDefaultCompileItems>
    <UserSecretsId>595958db-f6e9-463c-879e-e03615a37179</UserSecretsId></PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="**\*.cs" Exclude="Excluded.cs;$(DefaultItemExcludes)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

It's basically needed because whitespace is preserved when loading the XML doc now.

Ah, ok. My main concern is just that we don't actually know the incoming indentation level. If the user was indenting with 4 spaces, then we'll still end up messing that up. I don't really want us to add a whole complex new indentation engine here though :). This seems like a reasonable enough compromise to me now.
I agree 100%. I didn't want to go overboard with trying to determine the appropriate number of spaces.
